body_html:
Valentine’s Day messages in Spanish are a sweet way to surprise a Spanish-speaking partner, crush or friend on February 14. In Spanish, the day is San Valentín. If your partner or friends are Mexican, you will also hear el Día del Amor y la Amistad, the Day of Love and Friendship, because in Mexico and much of Latin America people celebrate friends, coworkers and family too, not just couples. Below are forty messages for every relationship, with English translations and notes on tone.

Quick answer
  • For your partner: ¡Feliz Día de San Valentín, mi amor!
  • For Mexican friends and family: ¡Feliz Día del Amor y la Amistad!
  • For friends: Feliz 14 de febrero, amiga. Gracias por estar siempre.
  • For a crush, keep it light: ¿Quieres ser mi San Valentín?
{{toc}}

Short Valentine’s Day messages in Spanish

  1. ¡Feliz San Valentín!
    Happy Valentine’s Day!
  2. ¡Feliz Día del Amor y la Amistad!
    Happy Day of Love and Friendship! (Mexico)
  3. ¡Feliz 14 de febrero!
    Happy February 14!
  4. Te quiero con todo mi corazón.
    I love you with all my heart.
  5. Eres mi persona favorita.
    You’re my favorite person.
  6. Contigo, todos los días son San Valentín.
    With you, every day is Valentine’s Day.

Romantic messages for your partner

  1. Feliz San Valentín al amor de mi vida.
    Happy Valentine’s Day to the love of my life.
  2. No necesito un día especial para decirte que te amo, pero hoy te lo digo dos veces.
    I don’t need a special day to tell you I love you, but today I’ll say it twice.
  3. Gracias por cada abrazo, cada risa y cada día a tu lado.
    Thank you for every hug, every laugh and every day by your side.
  4. Eres mi lugar favorito en el mundo.
    You’re my favorite place in the world.
  5. Si tuviera que elegir otra vez, te elegiría a ti.
    If I had to choose again, I would choose you.
  6. Mi corazón es tuyo, hoy y siempre.
    My heart is yours, today and always.
  7. Contigo aprendí que el amor bonito sí existe.
    With you I learned that beautiful love really exists.
  8. Te amo más de lo que las palabras pueden decir.
    I love you more than words can say.

For more romantic language, see {{link:te-quiero-vs-te-amo|te quiero vs te amo}} and {{link:spanish-terms-of-endearment|Spanish terms of endearment}}.

{{image:2}}

Messages for a crush or a new relationship

  1. ¿Quieres ser mi San Valentín?
    Will you be my Valentine?
  2. No sé si es San Valentín o eres tú, pero hoy estoy de muy buen humor.
    I don’t know if it’s Valentine’s Day or you, but I’m in a great mood today.
  3. Me encanta pasar tiempo contigo.
    I love spending time with you.
  4. ¿Te gustaría salir conmigo el sábado?
    Would you like to go out with me on Saturday?
  5. Pensé en ti y quise desearte un feliz 14 de febrero.
    I thought of you and wanted to wish you a happy February 14.

Keep it light at the start; te amo is far too strong for a first Valentine. See {{link:how-to-flirt-in-spanish|how to flirt in Spanish}} and {{link:first-date-in-spanish|first date in Spanish}}.

Día del Amor y la Amistad: messages for friends

  1. Feliz Día del Amor y la Amistad, amiga. Gracias por estar siempre.
    Happy Day of Love and Friendship, my friend. Thanks for always being there.
  2. Los amigos son la familia que uno elige. ¡Feliz 14!
    Friends are the family you choose. Happy 14th!
  3. Gracias por tantos años de risas y aventuras.
    Thank you for so many years of laughter and adventures.
  4. ¡Feliz día a mis amigos favoritos!
    Happy day to my favorite friends!
  5. Hoy celebro tener amigos como tú.
    Today I celebrate having friends like you.
  6. ¡Feliz Día del Amor y la Amistad, equipo! Gracias por todo su apoyo.
    Happy Day of Love and Friendship, team! Thanks for all your support.

If you work or study with Mexican or Central American colleagues, expect friendship messages too. In Mexican offices and schools, groups often do an intercambio de regalos (gift exchange) or amigo secreto (secret friend) on February 14. A short card with one of these lines is perfect.

{{book:love-slowly}}

Funny Valentine’s Day messages

  1. Eres el aguacate de mi tostada.
    You’re the avocado on my toast.
  2. Te quiero más que al café, y eso ya es decir mucho.
    I love you more than coffee, and that’s saying a lot.
  3. Feliz San Valentín a la persona que aguanta mis chistes malos.
    Happy Valentine’s Day to the person who puts up with my bad jokes.
  4. Para San Valentín quiero tres cosas: tú, pizza y una película.
    For Valentine’s Day I want three things: you, pizza and a movie.
  5. Feliz día, soltero. Hoy invito yo los tacos.
    Happy day, single friend. Tacos are on me today.

Messages if you are far apart

  1. Aunque estemos lejos, hoy te siento más cerca que nunca.
    Even though we’re far apart, today I feel closer to you than ever.
  2. Cuento los días para celebrar contigo en persona.
    I’m counting the days to celebrate with you in person.
  3. La distancia no cambia lo que siento.
    Distance doesn’t change what I feel.
  4. Te mando todo mi amor a través de la pantalla.
    Sending you all my love through the screen.

For more, see {{link:how-to-say-i-miss-you-in-spanish|how to say I miss you in Spanish}} and {{link:long-distance-relationship-spanish|long-distance relationship in Spanish}}.

{{image:3}}

Tips and common mistakes

  • Feliz Día de Valentín. The name is San Valentín: Feliz Día de San Valentín or simply Feliz San Valentín.
  • Te amo too soon. Use te quiero or me gustas early in a relationship.
  • Only writing to your partner. With Mexican friends and coworkers, a friendly message is often expected too.
  • Sé mi Valentín. Understood, but ¿Quieres ser mi San Valentín? sounds more natural.

Spanish capitalizes San Valentín as a proper name but not día in running text; see {{link:spanish-capitalization-rules|Spanish capitalization rules}} and the Diccionario panhispánico de dudas.

Final thoughts

Valentine’s Day messages in Spanish can be romantic, playful or simply grateful. Choose the tone that fits the relationship, remember that for Mexican friends and family it is a day of friendship too, and add one personal detail to make it yours. For more ready-to-send messages, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you say Happy Valentine’s Day in Spanish?
faq.a: ¡Feliz Día de San Valentín! or ¡Feliz San Valentín! In Mexico, ¡Feliz Día del Amor y la Amistad! is very common.

faq.q: What is Día del Amor y la Amistad?
faq.a: The Mexican and Latin American name for February 14, which celebrates both romantic love and friendship.

faq.q: How do you say “Will you be my Valentine?” in Spanish?
Should I send Valentine’s messages to Spanish-speaking friends?
faq.a: With Mexican and many Latin American friends and coworkers, yes. February 14 is also a day of friendship, so a short, friendly message is welcome.
